questions.sol: \(0<\tan\theta<1<\cot\theta\). With base \(<1\) a bigger exponent gives a smaller value: \(t_2<t_1<1\). With base \(>1\): \(1<t_3<t_4\).

questions.q: Let \(\dfrac\pi2<x<\pi\) be such that \(\cot x=\dfrac{-5}{\sqrt{11}}\). Then \(\left(\sin\dfrac{11x}2\right)(\sin6x-\cos6x)+\left(\cos\dfrac{11x}2\right)(\sin6x+\cos6x)\) is equal to
questions.sol: Grouping: \(\cos\left(6x-\frac{11x}2\right)+\sin\left(6x-\frac{11x}2\right)=\cos\frac x2+\sin\frac x2>0\). Its square is \(1+\sin x=1+\frac{\sqrt{11}}6=\dfrac{12+2\sqrt{11}}{12}=\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{11}+1}{2\sqrt3}\right)^2\).

Let \(\theta,\varphi\in[0,2\pi]\) be such that \(2\cos\theta(1-\sin\varphi)=\sin^2\theta\left(\tan\dfrac\theta2+\cot\dfrac\theta2\right)\cos\varphi-1\), \(\tan(2\pi-\theta)>0\) and \(-1<\sin\theta<-\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\). Then \(\varphi\) cannot satisfy
questions.sol: \(\tan\frac\theta2+\cot\frac\theta2=\frac2{\sin\theta}\), so the equation is \(2\cos\theta+1=2\sin(\theta+\varphi)\). The conditions give \(\frac{3\pi}2<\theta<\frac{5\pi}3\), so \(1<2\cos\theta+1<2\) and \(\frac12<\sin(\theta+\varphi)<1\): \(\frac{13\pi}6<\theta+\varphi<\frac{17\pi}6\). questions.q: Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be non-zero real numbers such that \(2(\cos\beta-\cos\alpha)+\cos\alpha\cos\beta=1\). Then which of the following is/are true?

For non-negative integer \(n\), let \(f(n)=\dfrac{\sum\limits_{k=0}^n\sin\left(\dfrac{k+1}{n+2}\pi\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{k+2}{n+2}\pi\right)}{\sum\limits_{k=0}^n\sin^2\left(\dfrac{k+1}{n+2}\pi\right)}\)
Assuming \(\cos^{-1}x\) takes values in \([0,\pi]\), which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.sol: With \(\theta=\frac\pi{n+2}\): numerator \(=\frac12\sum[\cos\theta-\cos(2k+3)\theta]=\frac{(n+2)\cos\theta}2\) and denominator \(=\frac12\sum[1-\cos(2k+2)\theta]=\frac{n+2}2\) (the cosine sums are \(-\cos\theta\) and \(-1\)). So \(f(n)=\cos\frac\pi{n+2}\). \(f(4)=\cos\frac\pi6\); \(\alpha=\tan\frac\pi8=\sqrt2-1\) satisfies \(\alpha^2+2\alpha-1=0\); \(\sin\left(7\cdot\frac\pi7\right)=0\); the limit is \(1\).

questions.q: Prove that \(\sin x\sin y\sin(x-y)+\sin y\sin z\sin(y-z)+\sin z\sin x\sin(z-x)+\sin(x-y)\sin(y-z)\sin(z-x)=0\)
questions.sol: \(\sin x\sin y\sin(x-y)=\frac12[\cos(x-y)-\cos(x+y)]\sin(x-y)=\frac14[\sin2(x-y)-\sin2x+\sin2y]\). Adding the three such terms, the \(\sin2x\) terms cancel, leaving \(\frac14[\sin2A+\sin2B+\sin2C]\) with \(A=x-y\), \(B=y-z\), \(C=z-x\), \(A+B+C=0\). For such angles \(\sin2A+\sin2B+\sin2C=-4\sin A\sin B\sin C\), which cancels the fourth term.

Prove that \(\tan\alpha+2\tan2\alpha+4\tan4\alpha+8\cot8\alpha=\cot\alpha\)
Using the relation \(2(1-\cos x)<x^2\), \(x\ne0\) or otherwise, prove that \(\sin(\tan x)\ge x\ \forall\ x\in\left[0,\dfrac\pi4\right]\)
Prove that \(\sin x+2x\ge\dfrac{3x\cdot(x+1)}\pi\ \forall\ x\in\left[0,\dfrac\pi2\right]\). (Justify the inequality, if any used).
questions.sol: \(f(x)=\sin x+2x-\dfrac{3x(x+1)}\pi\) has \(f''(x)=-\sin x-\dfrac6\pi<0\), so \(f\) is concave. \(f(0)=0\) and \(f\left(\frac\pi2\right)=\frac\pi4-\frac12>0\); a concave function lies above the chord joining its end points, so \(f\ge0\) on the interval.

questions.q: Find the range of values of \(t\) for which \(2\sin t=\dfrac{1-2x+5x^2}{3x^2-2x-1}\), \(t\in\left[-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right]\).
questions.sol: With \(y=2\sin t\): \((3y-5)x^2-2(y-1)x-(y+1)=0\) has real \(x\) iff \(y^2-y-1\ge0\), i.e. \(\sin t\le\frac{1-\sqrt5}4=-\sin\frac\pi{10}\) or \(\sin t\ge\frac{1+\sqrt5}4=\sin\frac{3\pi}{10}\).

questions.q: If \(\tan A=\dfrac{1-\cos B}{\sin B}\) then \(\tan2A=\tan B\)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{1-\cos B}{\sin B}=\tan\dfrac B2\), so \(\tan2A=\dfrac{2\tan\frac B2}{1-\tan^2\frac B2}=\tan B\).

questions.q: Let \(f:[0,2]\to R\) be the function defined by \(f(x)=(3-\sin(2\pi x))\sin\left(\pi x-\dfrac\pi4\right)-\sin\left(3\pi x+\dfrac\pi4\right)\). If \(\alpha,\beta\in[0,2]\) are such that \(\{x\in[0,2]:f(x)\ge0\}=[\alpha,\beta]\), then the value of \(\beta-\alpha\) is _____.
questions.sol: Put \(\theta=\pi x-\frac\pi4\): \(\sin2\pi x=\cos2\theta\) and \(\sin\left(3\pi x+\frac\pi4\right)=-\sin3\theta\). \(f=(3-\cos2\theta)\sin\theta+\sin3\theta=\sin\theta(5-2\sin^2\theta)\), which is \(\ge0\) iff \(\sin\theta\ge0\): \(\theta\in[0,\pi]\), i.e. \(x\in\left[\frac14,\frac54\right]\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be real numbers such that \(-\dfrac\pi4<\beta<0<\alpha<\dfrac\pi4\). If \(\sin(\alpha+\beta)=\dfrac13\) and \(\cos(\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac23\), then the greatest integer less than or equal to \(\left(\dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\beta}+\dfrac{\cos\beta}{\sin\alpha}+\dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\beta}+\dfrac{\sin\beta}{\cos\alpha}\right)^2\) is ______.
questions.sol: Pairing first with fourth and second with third: \(E=\frac12(\sin2\alpha+\sin2\beta)\cdot\dfrac{\cos(\alpha-\beta)}{\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\sin\beta\cos\beta}=\dfrac{4\sin(\alpha+\beta)\cos^2(\alpha-\beta)}{\sin2\alpha\sin2\beta}\). \(\sin2\alpha\sin2\beta=\frac12[\cos2(\alpha-\beta)-\cos2(\alpha+\beta)]=\frac12\left[-\frac19-\frac79\right]=-\frac49\). \(E=-\frac43\), \(E^2=\frac{16}9\).
